question: Which group of animals has a segmented spinal column together with a few primitive forms in which the backbone is represented by a notochord?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Vertebrata**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vertebrata** is the group of animals that have a segmented spinal column.
 
• This group includes not only advanced organisms with a developed backbone but also some primitive forms in which the backbone is represented by a notochord.
 
• The notochord is a flexible rod-like structure that forms the main support of the body in these primitive organisms.
 
• Examples of vertebrates include mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, and fish.
 
• The presence of a segmented spinal column is a key characteristic that differentiates vertebrates from other animal groups.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vertebrates** are part of the phylum Chordata, which is characterized by the presence of a notochord at some stage of development.
 
• The notochord is replaced by the vertebral column in most adult vertebrates, providing more structural support and protection for the spinal cord.
 
• Other distinguishing features of vertebrates include a well-developed brain, a closed circulatory system, and an endoskeleton made of bone or cartilage.
 
• The evolutionary development of the vertebral column has allowed vertebrates to become highly adaptable and occupy a wide range of ecological niches.
 
• Vertebrates are the most complex and diverse group of animals, with over 66,000 species described to date.
